question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-on user-scoped memory isolation contract in memory-core, and what upgrade/security semantics must be required before merge?
rationale: This PR defines a privacy boundary, adds config/default surface, changes persisted memory partitioning, and affects existing shared-memory behavior, so maintainer intent is needed beyond mechanical code repair.

options.title: Repair the isolation contract before merge
options.body: Require absent-config default-on behavior, remove or implement every accepted option, resolve conflicts, and attach redacted builtin plus QMD two-user proof before landing.

options.title: Narrow to an explicit opt-in experiment
options.body: Keep existing shared behavior as the upgrade default and expose user isolation only behind a documented opt-in until migration and legacy-memory policy are settled.

options.title: Pause this branch for canonical design
options.body: Keep the open canonical tracker as the owner and avoid merging this branch until maintainers settle the identity, migration, and proof requirements.

recommendation.title: Repair the isolation contract before merge
recommendation.body: Require absent-config default-on behavior, remove or implement every accepted option, resolve conflicts, and attach redacted builtin plus QMD two-user proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main work and proof on memory-core internals make this the best available owner for deciding the current implementation boundary.
